YYForce plans service robots at two Singapore on Stevens hotels

Deliveries, cleaning and concierge support come first; humanoid housekeeping remains a later research programme.

YYForce / PRNewswire ↗13 October 2026English editorial summary
Story

A two-hotel operating environment

YYForce, Novotel Singapore on Stevens and Mercure Singapore on Stevens announced a partnership across 772 guestrooms, restaurants and event spaces. The service-robot rollout is confirmed, but the release explicitly says deployment has not begun.

Prepare the building interfaces

Phase one covers specialist robots for guest deliveries, food-and-beverage transport, scheduled cleaning and concierge directions. Lift integration, routes, networking and arrival notifications must be prepared, with tasks matched to capability and technical readiness.

Savings are projections

A pre-deployment model projects roughly 10% lower monthly costs in selected operations, including robot costs; this is not a measured outcome. Later research would use permitted observations of housekeeping and banquet work, not establish autonomous cleaning of occupied guestrooms.
